name: Ragi Sangati
subtitle: finger millet and rice pounded into a smooth ball, the working staple of Rayalaseema

ingredients.note: cooked soft with the millet, not separately

prepNotes: Sangati is eaten with a hot, thin curry, usually natu kodi pulusu or a chilli and onion chutney. On its own it is deliberately plain.
The pounding is the technique. A whisk gives lumps; a sturdy wooden spoon and some force gives the smooth, heavy texture the dish is named for.

steps.text: Boil the rice in the water until completely soft and collapsing, about 20 minutes. Do not drain it.
Lower the heat. Rain the ragi flour in with one hand while stirring hard with the other.
steps.tip: All at once and you get a lump you will never break up.

steps.text: Cook 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until it pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Take it off the heat and pound it against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon until glossy and smooth, about 3 minutes.
Wet your hands and shape into balls. Serve at once with a hot curry.
steps.tip: It sets firm as it cools, so shape while hot.

storage: Best eaten straight away. It keeps a day refrigerated but sets hard; steam it briefly to soften rather than microwaving, which dries the surface.
